title: Counterexamples to a conjectured waiting-time bound on entropy production in periodically driven Markov networks
oneLine: A forward-only waiting-time statistic conjectured to be a lower bound on the entropy production of periodically driven systems can report dissipation where there is none, and can overstate it by more than 31 per cent (certified) in the very model class where the conjecture was tested.
abstract: Entropy production measures how far a small system, such as a molecular motor, a single molecule pulled in an experiment or a colloid in a driven optical trap, is from equilibrium. When only some transitions are visible, it is estimated from the visible jumps and the waiting times between them. For periodically driven Markov networks, Maier, Degünther, van der Meer and Seifert (Journal of Statistical Physics 191, 104, 2024) conjectured that a statistic computed from the forward experiment alone, with the phase of the drive averaged out, never exceeds the true entropy production. This candidate shows that the conjecture is false. In a three-state network with one observed edge, two hidden barriers modulated out of phase keep the system in equilibrium at every instant, so the entropy production is exactly zero, while the statistic is strictly positive (analytic proof; about 1e-5 per unit time). In the class with fixed kinetic prefactors, where the conjecture was tested numerically, small-amplitude driving provably obeys the bound, but slow large-amplitude driving violates it: interval arithmetic certifies a ratio of at least 1.3179 for a switching protocol, smooth counterexamples exist, and smooth protocols reach about 2 numerically. The statistic is nonnegative and, at equilibrium, measures how distinguishable the protocol is from its time reverse. For a fixed network and fastest rate its excess grows at most like the logarithm of one over the slowest rate, and that growth is attained. Estimators that use the reversed protocol remain valid. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Zero-dissipation counterexample (Theorem 3.1, proof with exact sign certificate): in a three-state network observed only on the edge 1–2, hidden barriers 1 + ε cos ωt and 1 + ε sin ωt keep every rate equal to its reverse, so σ = 0, but the forward-only phase-averaged statistic S of Maier et al. is strictly positive (S ≈ 1.13×10⁻⁵ per unit time at ε = 1/2, ω = 1). The upper inequality of their conjecture fails.

Fixed-prefactor class, where the conjecture was tested: small-amplitude driving obeys S < σ (Theorem 4.1, proof); a 128-piece switching protocol with A = 4, ω = 1/20 has S ≥ 0.0036867 > σ = 0.0027973, a ratio of at least 1.3179 (Theorem 4.2, certified by interval arithmetic); smooth counterexamples exist (Corollary 4.3); smooth circular protocols reach S/σ ≈ 2.03 (numerical).

What S measures (proofs): S = D(Q‖Q^R) − D(r‖r̄) ≥ 0; at equilibrium the reversed-protocol estimator is zero and S = D(Q‖Q̃) measures how distinguishable the protocol is from its time reverse. Time-symmetric driving gives S = 0 at equilibrium (proof); with a cycle affinity a numerical witness has S ≈ 1.10 σ.

Size of the error (proofs): S ≤ K[(m+1) log(k_max/k_min) + log m! + m d] + R_max for every network, so at fixed graph and fastest rate the excess grows at most like log(1/k_min); a pulse family with σ = 0 attains that growth. No logarithmic claim is made as k_max grows.
Safe alternatives: the reversed-protocol estimator of Maier et al. and its coarse-grainings, their σ_pk estimator, and the corrected inequality of Harunari, Fiore and Barato remain valid.

narration: When a waiting-time test sees dissipation that is not there. An Evidence Press briefing. Tiny machines, such as molecular motors in cells or beads held in laser traps, constantly exchange energy with their surroundings. Physicists measure how far such a system is from equilibrium by its entropy production: the rate at which it turns energy into heat. Usually only a few of the system's jumps can be seen, so researchers try to infer entropy production from the visible jumps and the waiting times between them. In 2024, Maier, Degünther, van der Meer and Seifert proposed a convenient statistic for systems driven by a repeating rhythm. It needs only the ordinary experiment, not a second experiment with the rhythm run backwards. After testing more than a hundred thousand random models, they conjectured that it never overstates the true value. This release shows that the conjecture is false. In a three-state model, two hidden energy barriers are raised and lowered out of step. The system stays in equilibrium at every instant, so it dissipates nothing. Yet the visible waiting times look different in the two directions, because the drive makes the hidden barriers open in a fixed order. The statistic reads this as dissipation. The effect in this example is very small. But in the class of models the conjecture's authors tested, weak driving is always safe, while slow, strong driving overstates dissipation, by at least thirty-one per cent in one case certified with interval arithmetic, and by about a factor of two in numerical examples. Estimators that use the reversed rhythm remain valid. The practical lesson is not to report this forward-only statistic as a lower bound on dissipation. These are mathematical results about model systems, not experiments. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, not peer reviewed or independently reproduced. Published on 21 October 2026, its paper and evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

corrections.summary: Corrected a sentence in §10 (“What fails and why”) that understated the paper's own results. The archived text says the statistic has been proved harmless “only for time-symmetric protocols at equilibrium”. Theorem 4.1 also proves that, in the fixed-prefactor class, every nonconstant small-amplitude periodic driving around an equilibrium satisfies $\hat S<\sigma$, with $\hat S/\sigma=O(A^2)$, as the abstract states.
corrections.detail: The theorems, certificates and the practical advice not to report the statistic as a dissipation bound are unchanged. The archived PDF, version DOI and repository tag are unchanged; the erratum is recorded here and in the repository's CORRECTIONS.md on its main branch.

decisionObject.description: A refutation of the upper inequality in the Maier et al. (2024) conjecture for the forward-only phase-averaged waiting-time statistic, with a certified violation in the fixed-prefactor class, a logarithmic error bound and a map of which estimators remain safe.
decisionObject.scope: Finite continuous-time Markov jump processes with periodic rates and a symmetric set of observed transitions, as in Maier et al.; mathematical results about model networks, not an experimental claim.
